First, we find the derivative of $f(t)$ by differentiating each component.

$$
{f}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{cos}^{2}⁡t)\,\,\,\, \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{sin}⁡t-5)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ -6\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]
$$

Next, we calculate ${f}^{″}(t)$ by differentiating ${f}^{′}(t):$

$$
{f}^{″}(t)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-6\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ -6({cos}^{2}⁡t-{sin}^{2}⁡t) \\ -4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ -6\operatorname{cos}⁡2t \\ -4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, we find ${f}^{″}(\pi )$ by substituting $t=\pi $ into the above:

$$
{f}^{″}(\pi )=[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi -\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi  \\ -6\operatorname{cos}⁡2\pi  \\ -4\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi \end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-(-1)-0 \\ -6\cdot 1 \\ -4\cdot 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -6 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$
